questions.question: Which class category should you choose for a domain object that must be saved to the database and reopened later by ID?

options.text: %Registered
%SerialObject
%Persistent
%DataType

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%Persistent` stores data in the IRIS database and provides an object ID, so it can be saved and reopened later.

questions.question: A validator object is used only during one request and should never be stored. Which superclass is the best fit?

options.text: %Persistent
%Registered
%SerialObject
%XML.Adaptor

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%Registered` is for in-memory helper or service objects that do not need persistence.

questions.question: Which statement best describes `%SerialObject`?

options.text: It has its own independent `%ID` and table.
It is embedded inside a parent object and has no standalone ID.
It can only contain numeric properties.
It is a memory-only object just like `%Registered`.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%SerialObject` is stored inline with its parent and cannot be opened independently by ID.

questions.question: What is true about a class defined with `[ Abstract ]`?

options.text: It is automatically persisted without `%Save()`.
It can be instantiated but not subclassed.
It is intended as a base class and cannot be instantiated directly.
It must extend `%Registered`.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — an abstract class is used to define shared structure or behavior for subclasses and is not instantiated directly.

questions.question: Which mixin adds JSON import and export support to a class?

options.text: %JSON.Adaptor
%SerialObject
%DataType
%Library.DynamicObject

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%JSON.Adaptor` adds methods such as `%JSONExport()` and `%JSONImport()`.

questions.question: You want to store an address inside `MyApp.Person` without creating a separate ID for the address. Which design is most appropriate?

options.text: Make both classes `%Persistent` and save them separately.
Use `%SerialObject` for the address and embed it in the person.
Use `%Registered` for the address and call `%Save()` on it.
Use `[ Abstract ]` for the address and instantiate it directly.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson describes `%SerialObject` as the correct choice when related fields should be stored inline inside a parent object.

questions.question: Which statements about `%Persistent` are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: `%Save()` returns a `%Status`.
`%OpenId(id)` opens an object by its ID.
`%KillExtent()` deletes all instances of the class.
`%Persistent` objects never have an object ID.
`%Persistent` data exists only in process memory.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%Persistent` objects have IDs, are stored in the database, and use methods like `%Save()`, `%OpenId()`, and `%KillExtent()`.

questions.question: Which statements about `%Registered`, `%SerialObject`, and abstract classes are correct? (select all that apply)

options.text: `%Registered` exists only in memory.
`%SerialObject` can be opened independently with `%OpenId()`.
An abstract class is intended to be subclassed rather than instantiated directly.
`%SerialObject` is saved together with its parent object.
`%Registered` automatically persists when the process ends.

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%Registered` is memory-only, `%SerialObject` is embedded in its parent, and abstract classes define shared behavior without direct instantiation.

questions.question: What does the following code print after `p.%Rollback()` runs?
questions.code:
SET p = ##class(MyApp.Person).%OpenId(1)
SET p.Name = "New Name"
DO p.%Rollback()
WRITE p.%IsModified(), !

options.text: "New Name"
An automatic save occurs, so it prints the ID

questions.explanation: T1.2 — the lesson shows `%Rollback()` discarding in-memory changes, so `%IsModified()` becomes 0 afterward.

questions.question: Which scenarios are good fits for `%Registered`? (select all that apply)

options.text: A request-time validator object
A DTO used only to pass temporary data between methods
A helper service object with no persistence requirement
A patient record that must be stored permanently and reopened by ID
An embedded address object stored inside a persistent parent

questions.explanation: T1.2 — `%Registered` is for temporary in-memory helpers or DTO-style objects, not for persistent records or embedded serial objects.
